title: Applied Intelligent Document Processing for Procurement Automation: An OCR-Assisted LLM Framework for Supplier Quotation Emails
content: Supplier quotation emails often contain product-related information distributed across unstructured email bodies, HTML tables, PDF files, scanned documents, and spreadsheet attachments. This heterogeneity makes rule-based and template-dependent extraction pipelines difficult to maintain in real-world procurement workflows. This study presents an OCR-assisted and attachment-aware large language model framework for structured product information extraction from supplier quotation emails. The proposed framework combines email parsing, OCR/PDF text extraction, structured context construction, schema-constrained prompting, domain adaptation with LoRA, and database-assisted response generation. The system is designed for on-premise processing of industrial procurement data and is evaluated using field-level precision, recall, F1-score, JSON validity, hallucination behavior, and processing latency. Instead of treating OCR, language modeling, and response generation as isolated modules, the framework organizes them into a unified workflow that processes both email body content and attachment-derived text. The results and analysis aim to clarify the practical value and limitations of domain-adapted open-source LLMs for enterprise procurement automation.
